trust_decision.summary: Which key wraps an OIDC/WebAuthn user's data-encryption key at rest is decided in UserCrypto.deriveOIDCSystemKey/deriveWebAuthnSystemKey. When OIDC_SYSTEM_SECRET/WEBAUTHN_SYSTEM_SECRET are unset, both fall back to a constant string, so anyone with a copy of the settings table can rebuild the key from the userId.

landing_point.why: The advisory names a hardcoded default key for OIDC/WebAuthn users. A grep for the default secret string lands straight on the two derive functions.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /users/oidc/callback, first OIDC login (setupOIDCUserEncryption new-wrap branch)

POST /users/login dual-auth unlock (src/backend/database/routes/users.ts:1658); also POST /database/export (src/backend/database/database.ts:633), POST /database/import (src/backend/database/database.ts:1201), POST /ldap/login (src/backend/database/routes/ldap-auth-routes.ts:420)
private key derivation shared by all of the above

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All changed sites are in src/backend/utils/user-crypto.ts. The only stored-state element is the existing wraps in the settings table (src/backend/utils/user-crypto.ts:659,699,719). They must be re-wrapped on read (fix.diff:106385-106418), but that work stays inside the same file.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Wraps already stored under the default key look like 'legacy data that operators should re-key themselves'. A solver could swap in the per-install key for new wraps and argue that migrating existing settings rows, or re-wrapping dormant users who never log in, is out of scope for a key-derivation fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Existing OIDC/WebAuthn users whose DEK was wrapped under the default secret must still unlock their credentials, and deployments that set OIDC_SYSTEM_SECRET/WEBAUTHN_SYSTEM_SECRET (WebAuthn falls back to the OIDC secret) must keep their derivation. A fix that only swaps the key, or that drops the env path, locks every existing SSO/passkey user out of their stored SSH credentials.

O6_input_shapes: oidc wrap in primary slot user_encrypted_dek_<id> (src/backend/utils/user-crypto.ts:659)
oidc wrap in dual-auth slot user_encrypted_dek_oidc_<id> (src/backend/utils/user-crypto.ts:699)
legacy-default wrap vs new wrap on decrypt (fix.diff:106395-106400)

O7_producer.where: Wraps are produced inside the same class (encryptDEK, src/backend/utils/user-crypto.ts:587-602) and stored via settings rows (src/backend/utils/user-crypto.ts:655-675). No separate schema, serializer or config loader is involved.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Settings rows already wrapped under the default key, for users who never log in again, are not re-wrapped by 401ec7e (it migrates lazily on decrypt only). A later boot-time migration in the companion commit covers them.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Re-keying data at rest looks like an operator migration task rather than a code fix, and the lazy path already 'handles' it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; the boot migration lives in a new module src/backend/utils/crypto-migration/dek-migration.ts (fix.diff:63482-63573)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A write path for the legacy v1 DB-file format that still uses the constant seed when DB_FILE_KEY is unset.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The constant-seed v1 decrypt path already exists next to the v2 path. A 'compatibility export' writing v1 is a plausible maintainer addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A constant fallback in place of the random key when neither GUACAMOLE_ENCRYPTION_KEY nor JWT_SECRET is set.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The function already chains env fallbacks. A fixed string 'so tokens survive restarts' mirrors the user-crypto pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The session dataKeyWrap derived from a default secret instead of SystemCrypto.getEncryptionKey.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a second DEK-wrapping implementation in another file. A planted variant would be a distance-type second implementation of the same wrap.

O9_family: crypto misuse: hardcoded/default key (CWE-321) wrapping per-user data keys at rest

O10_build.toolchain: Node >=22.12, npm >=11, tsc + vite, vitest; native better-sqlite3 (package.json:8-11,22,28)
O10_build.project_tests: No user-crypto unit test at the pinned commit. The neighbouring test is src/backend/utils/field-crypto.test.ts. The fix's dek-migration tests arrive only with ddbdd5c.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the constant fallback with SystemCrypto.getEncryptionKey() in both derive functions without a legacy-decrypt fallback, which breaks unlock for every existing OIDC/WebAuthn user.

out_of_scope_notes: POST /database/export (src/backend/database/database.ts:1077-1090) copies all settings rows, including other users' DEK wraps, into any authenticated user's export. This is access control, not this advisory's property.
Legacy v1 DB-file decrypt uses a constant seed when DB_FILE_KEY is unset (src/backend/utils/database-file-encryption.ts:294-296). It is decrypt-only and a different sink.
Math.random is used for TOTP backup codes (src/backend/database/routes/user-totp-routes.ts:257,464). Separate weakness, not pursued.
unverified: Fix commit ddbdd5c is a release-sized change (~106k diff lines) that deletes user-crypto.ts entirely (fix.diff:67447-67452) and replaces it with a new crypto-migration layer. The task would have to be based on 401ec7e alone; ddbdd5c was not reviewed beyond the default-key migration.

single_site was not flagged because O8 has an entry, but it is effectively near-single-site: 8 call sites funnel through two private derive functions in one file, and the O8 entry (dormant-user rewrap) is arguably a residual rather than a separate route.
Latest release not provided, so present_in_latest is unknown.
